t: #3621 Number of Integers With Popcount-Depth Equal to K I
o: The popcount-depth of x is the number of popcount iterations needed to reach 1 (depth 0 only for x = 1). Since x <= 1e15 has at most ~50 bits, popcount(x) <= 50, so depths are tiny and we can precompute depth[c] for every possible popcount c in 0..50. Then the answer is a sum over c of (numbers <= n with popcount exactly c) restricted to c whose induced depth equals k, computed with a standard digit DP / binomial counting over the bits of n.
k: depth(x) = 0 if x = 1, else 1 + depth(popcount(x)); only the popcount of x matters, so bucket by c = popcount.
Precompute depth for c in 0..50 (chain length is at most ~6).
Count numbers <= n with a given popcount via the classic 'place a 0 at a set bit, freely choose lower bits' combinatorial scan.

a.n: Approach 1: Bucket by popcount + binomial digit counting
a.i: For each candidate popcount c whose depth chain hits k, count integers in [1, n] with popcount c by scanning bits of n from high to low: whenever the bit is 1, choosing 0 there leaves (bit index) free positions to place the remaining ones, contributing C(bitIndex, remaining). Finally include n itself if its popcount equals c. Special cases: k = 0 means only x = 1; for k >= 1 subtract the x = 1 contribution when c = 1.
s: Precompute d[c] = popcount-depth of the integer c for c in 0..50.
Implement count(m, c): numbers in [1, m] with popcount exactly c, via the binomial bit scan.
If k == 0 return 1 (only x = 1, and n >= 1).
Otherwise sum count(n, c) over all c with 1 + d[c] == k, then subtract 1 if c = 1 contributed (excluding x = 1).
a.t: O(60 * 60) precomputation plus O(60 * 60) per query-free run — effectively constant; the counting scan is O(bits * k).
a.sp: O(1) beyond a few arrays of size 60.

w: The crucial observation is that depth depends only on popcount, collapsing the problem to 50 buckets. Pitfalls: forgetting x = 1 has depth 0 (subtract it for k = 1), c = 0 never occurs since x >= 1, and verifying with n = 4, k = 1 (answer 2) and n = 7, k = 2 (answer 3). Follow-up: the hard version asks the same over ranges with multiple queries — precompute prefix counts per depth.
